Production PIXEL ART for the existing Sproto fighting game. Crisp stepped pixels, dark outlines, compact limited-color shading. Not smooth vector or painterly art. Each cell contains exactly ONE complete actor facing RIGHT, consistent three-quarter side view. Preserve the reference identity, facial shape, exact eye count, colors, clothing, accessories and slender long torso. Same head, torso and limb proportions in every frame. Exactly two arms and two legs per actor, legs rooted at the LOWEST pelvis below the belly. Low hip, chambered knee and connected ankle for every kick. Never attach legs to the chest. Keep all limbs and feet wholly inside their own cell with generous empty margins; no clipping. Flat solid pure MAGENTA #ff00ff background, no grid lines, labels, shadows, trails, floating particles or weapons. Worn/held identity accessories must remain attached to body or hand. Extend cropped lower bodies conservatively using matching skin/clothing colors and simple shoes. Complete separate body drawings; no limb cutouts. Both feet need readable soles. No extra subjects.

IDENTITY: Erik Stevens Sproto is the ONE BLUE SPROTO in reference image 1. Preserve the broad cobalt-blue head, large swept RED top/back spikes, relaxed yellow eyes with large BLACK pupils and small white highlights, subtle brow and eyelid creases, very large rounded RED nose, broad RED smiling muzzle/lips and long clean-shaven blue neck. No beard, hair, hat or red irises. He wears FORMAL BUSINESS CLOTHES WITH A NECKTIE. Preserve the YELLOW collared dress shirt and RED long necktie from the source; extend the cropped outfit as a tailored dark navy suit jacket with open front, matching dark navy formal trousers and polished simple black dress shoes. The red tie has a small triangular knot under the shirt collar and a clear long narrow tie blade reaching down the shirt front; it is NOT a bow tie, scarf or loose ribbon. The YELLOW shirt and RED NECKTIE stay clearly visible in EVERY pose. The tie is attached at the collar and stays neatly against the torso, never a limb or floating object. Slim yellow shirt cuffs, blue bare hands with visible fingers. No boxing gloves or weapons. Exact same suit, shirt, tie colors and head proportions in every cell. Formal, confident, composed bearing; keep face recognizable. Image 1 specifies the original face, yellow collar and red tie. Image 2 is the approved full-body formal outfit: copy the EXACT navy suit, YELLOW dress shirt, long RED NECKTIE, blue bare hands and black dress shoes. The red tie remains tied at the collar and lies against the chest, visible inside the open jacket. Never change it to a bow tie, remove it, make it yellow or let it become a detached object. Match the head proportions and red top/back spikes exactly.

Exactly EIGHT separate full-body drawings in a regular 4-column by 2-row grid. A continuous guarded fighting footwork loop, NOT a run. Upper body stays calm, head/torso size constant, hips stay at the same height and same x center. Both fists remain raised. Feet are clearly different on adjacent frames: 0 near foot forward grounded/far foot back grounded; 1 transfer weight to near sole, far heel lifts; 2 far knee passes under low pelvis with far foot lifted; 3 far foot reaches forward while near sole still supports; 4 far foot forward grounded/near foot back grounded; 5 transfer weight to far sole, near heel lifts; 6 near knee passes under low pelvis with near foot lifted; 7 near foot reaches forward ready to plant. No feet crossing through one another, no sliding torso, no detached hips. Each frame has at least one clearly grounded foot. Last frame loops to first. Same complete body and clothing as the combat reference.
 Clothing has coherent shoulder, elbow, hip and knee folds. The necktie follows the torso without disappearing, detaching or changing into a bow tie during punches, kicks, jumps, grabs and reactions. Do not hide the yellow shirt and red tie behind a closed jacket. No labels, logos or extra subjects. Strict exact count and generous magenta gutters around all complete figures.
